scope: Recent case literature on drug-induced lupus erythematosus.

keyRecommendations.text: Among 29 recent case reports, anti-TNF drugs were the most frequent (41.7%) among systemic DILE reports.
keyRecommendations.population: Published DILE cases in the review window

keyRecommendations.text: Chemotherapeutic drugs were the most common class (54.5%) in the subacute cutaneous lupus cases, with a higher incidence in females.
keyRecommendations.population: Subacute cutaneous DILE cases in the review

keyRecommendations.text: Stopping the culprit drug usually improves the drug-induced manifestations.

clinicalBottomLine: Recognise an expanding list of culprit drugs, including anti-TNF agents in recent systemic cases, and stop the drug. Procainamide and hydralazine are discussed as NET inducers, not as a ranked incidence list.
notableCaveats: The 41.7% and 54.5% figures describe this review's recent case reports, not lifetime population incidence.
